economy.summary: His campaign says he will fight to raise the minimum wage and strengthen worker protections, and supports policies to help small business owners start up, grow, and hire. Lists affordable utilities and family-sustaining jobs among his kitchen-table priorities.
economy.short: Supports raising minimum wage, worker protections, small business growth.

taxes.summary: His campaign supports protecting and enhancing targeted tax-relief programs for senior citizens, saying tax relief should help older Pennsylvanians stay in their homes and neighborhoods.
taxes.short: Supports targeted tax relief helping seniors stay in homes.

education.summary: Says he will fight to make sure classrooms have the resources to give every child a fair shot, calling public schools the backbone of every strong community. A 34-year public school teacher and former president of the Pennsylvania State Education Association.
education.short: Supports resourcing public school classrooms; former teacher and PSEA president.

healthcare.summary: His campaign says he will work to protect and strengthen programs seniors count on, naming Medicare and SNAP, and to support seniors retiring with dignity and security; these are federal programs his campaign lists as state-level priorities.
healthcare.short: Supports protecting Medicare and SNAP programs for seniors.

economy.summary: His official legislative biography lists boosting job creation among his top priorities and cites his work leading opposition to a state proposal to toll interstate bridges.
economy.short: Lists job creation as priority; opposed interstate bridge tolling.

taxes.summary: Sponsored legislation to gradually reduce Pennsylvania's corporate net income tax from 9.99 percent to 4.99 percent over five years, saying lowering it would attract new job creators and encourage existing employers to grow and hire.
taxes.short: Sponsored gradual corporate net income tax reduction to attract employers.

abortion.summary: In July 2022 voted for Senate Bill 106, a proposed state constitutional amendment providing that there is no constitutional right to taxpayer-funded abortion or other right relating to abortion; the measure passed the House 107-92.
abortion.short: Voted for amendment stating no constitutional right to abortion.

education.summary: Championed a $10 million state budget investment in evidence-based reading instruction, noting every school will now be required to use it, and framed the literacy investment as reducing future spending on remediation and special education. His biography also cites school safety grant and student mental health programs he sponsored.
education.short: Championed evidence-based reading instruction funding and school safety grants.

healthcare.summary: Sponsored legislation, first introduced in January 2025, calling for the creation of a state eating disorders task force; the initiative led to eating disorder awareness education provisions in the public school code.
healthcare.short: Sponsored bill creating state eating disorders task force.

energy.summary: Supported Pennsylvania's exit from the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative in the 2025-26 state budget, calling RGGI an energy tax that hurt working families and drove up electricity bills, and saying withdrawal protects jobs and helps keep utility costs down.
energy.short: Supported RGGI exit, calling it an energy tax.

guns.summary: In November 2021 voted for Senate Bill 565, which would have removed the license requirement for carrying a concealed firearm in Pennsylvania; the bill passed the House 107-92 and was vetoed by the governor.
guns.short: Voted to remove license requirement for concealed firearm carry.
